preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 5000 for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit()) and len(stdin.split()) == 2 + n
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 50) and k (1 ≤ k ≤ 5000). The second line contains exactly n integers, each either 50 or 100, representing the weights of the people.

preconditions.expression: n == len([w for w in stdin.split()[2:] if w.isdigit()])
preconditions.description: The number of weights matches the given n.

preconditions.expression: all(w in {50, 100} for w in [int(x) for x in stdin.split()[2:] if x.isdigit()])
preconditions.description: Each weight is either 50 or 100 kilograms.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is either -1 (impossible) or a positive integer representing the minimum number of boat rides required to transport everyone to the other side.
The second line of stdout is either 0 (if impossible) or the number of ways modulo 10^9 + 7 to transport everyone in the minimum number of rides.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.split()[0]) == -1 or (int(stdout.split()[0]) >= 1 and all(sum(subset) <= k for subset in possible_subsets) and all(len(subset) >= 1 for subset in possible_subsets))
postconditions.description: If the answer is not -1, there exists at least one valid sequence of boat rides (each with total weight ≤ k and at least one person) that transports everyone to the other side in the minimum number of rides. `possible_subsets` is the set of all valid subsets of people that can be transported in a single ride (including return trips).

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.split()[0]) == -1 or (int(stdout.split()[0]) == min_rides and int(stdout.split()[1]) == count_ways % 1000000007)
postconditions.description: If the answer is not -1, `min_rides` is the minimum number of boat rides required to transport everyone to the other side, and `count_ways` is the number of distinct ways to achieve this (mod 10^9 + 7).
